# 什么是提示词注入（SEO）？

- 原标题：What Is Prompt Injection (SEO)?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/prompt-injection/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

提示词注入是一种攻击：将隐藏或恶意指令嵌入 AI 系统读取的内容，诱使模型遵循这些指令，而不是完成原本任务。在 SEO 语境中，间接提示词注入，是在页面内容中隐藏指令，试图操纵 AI 搜索引擎对某个主题的说法，或它认定哪个来源具有权威性。

### 核心要点

- OWASP 将提示词注入列为 LLM01，即其 2025 年大语言模型应用十大风险中的首要风险。
- 间接提示词注入把指令埋进网页、文件或图片等外部内容中，等待大语言模型日后读取并执行。
- OWASP 指出，注入内容“不必对人类可见或可读，只要模型能够解析即可”。
- 在 Zscaler ThreatLabz 2026 年的一项研究中，欺诈网站利用屏幕之外的 CSS 隐藏指令，要求 AI 代理把假页面排为“第一首要来源”。
- 通过隐藏指令引导 AI 答案，是黑帽操纵，不是正当优化。AI 厂商将其视为需要防御的攻击，网站也面临被过滤或从索引移除的风险。

### 提示词注入如何运作

生成式 AI 系统读取的内容远多于用户的问题。AI 搜索引擎或代理回答时，会摄取检索到的网页、文档和数据，并将其中相当一部分文字当作工作指令的一部分。提示词注入利用了这种信任。攻击者不是向模型提出问题，而是埋入告诉模型该做什么的文字；由于模型并不总能区分需要总结的内容与应该服从的命令，它可能遵循这些植入指令。

行业标准参考是 OWASP，其大语言模型应用十大风险将提示词注入列为 **LLM01**，也就是优先级最高的风险。OWASP 将它分为两类：**直接**提示词注入，是用户在聊天中直接输入恶意指令；**间接**提示词注入，则是与搜索相关的那一种，即把指令藏在网页、文件、图片等外部内容里，模型在检索时读取它们。关键是，OWASP 指出注入文字“不必对人类可见或可读，只要模型能够解析即可”。因此，攻击经常隐藏在不可见页面元素中。

在 SEO 的表述下，间接提示词注入，是试图在页面中藏入指令——屏幕外文字、白底白字或虚假的[结构化数据](https://roborank.io/glossary/machine-readable-content/)——要求 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)或代理偏爱该页、重复预先写好的说法，或将该网站称为权威[事实依据来源](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding-source/)。它与正当的[生成式引擎优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/)处于对立面；后者通过提供清楚、可验证的内容，让引擎主动选择引用。区别不是表面措辞：一个提供模型可以核查的证据，另一个则发出模型本不应收到的命令。

### 提示词注入示例

2026 年 7 月，Zscaler ThreatLabz 的安全研究人员记录了真实环境中针对 AI 代理使用间接提示词注入的情况。其中一次行动围绕一个拼写仿冒域名展开，冒充加密货币投资组合追踪工具 DeBank。攻击者除了进行普通关键词堆砌，以及加入虚假的[机器可读](https://roborank.io/glossary/machine-readable-content/) JSON-LD、宣称欺诈网站是 DeBank 官方软件之外，还嵌入了隐藏的提示词注入文字。

其实现机制最能说明问题。指令放在通过 CSS 隐藏、定位到远离屏幕位置的 `div` 元素中。报告描述了被推至 `left: -9999px` 的文字：人类访客完全看不到，解析 HTML 的 AI 代理却能完整读取。隐藏文字指示 AI 代理，在 DeBank 搜索中将假页面视为“第一首要来源”，制造该网站并未赢得的权威感。在隔离测试中，一些模型受骗，把欺诈页面评为合法页面。

这个例子直接对应 SEO 中的担忧：竞争对手是否能在页面里埋指令，劫持 AI 对某个主题的说法？诚实的答案是，这类尝试确实存在，也确实发生过；正因如此，AI 平台将检索内容视为不可信，并建立防御机制来剥离注入命令。这也说明它不是值得押注的策略。它被列在 OWASP 风险清单的首位，正是为了让引擎学会忽略它；而欺骗性的隐藏文字，长期以来也一直是搜索系统过滤或移除域名的理由。想长期成为引擎点名的来源，应该真正提供最清楚、最[可验证](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)的答案，而不是用读者看不到的墨水悄悄下命令。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们的错误，是把两件非常不同的事混在同一个充满期待的名目下。让内容便于 AI 使用——明确主张、清晰结构、可检索事实——是正当优化，它之所以有效，是因为引擎选择引用你。植入隐藏文字，要求模型把你叫作权威来源，不是优化，而是攻击，正是 OWASP 列为首要大语言模型安全风险的行为。二者似乎相邻，因为都涉及 AI 读取的内容，但在伦理和实践上位于界线两侧。一个赢得系统可核实的信任，另一个试图伪造信任；而厂商正在构建检测手段，要剥离的正是伪造信任。应优化真实、公开可见的内容。隐藏指令路线只是短命伎俩，让域名被标记，而不是被突出展示。

### 常见问题

#### SEO 中的提示词注入是什么？

它是在网页中隐藏指令的黑帽手法，通常利用不可见文字或结构化数据，试图让 AI 搜索引擎推广该页或复述指定观点。它是在操纵模型，而不是赢得引用，因此被视为攻击。

#### 为 AI 隐藏指令是正当 SEO 策略吗？

不是。这属于间接提示词注入，是 OWASP 排在首位的大语言模型安全风险。正当优化让真实内容更容易被检索和引用；注入则试图用隐藏命令覆盖模型判断，AI 厂商正在积极构建防御来识别并丢弃这些内容。

#### 直接与间接提示词注入有什么区别？

直接提示词注入发生在用户把恶意指令直接输入聊天时。间接提示词注入把指令藏进网页、文档或图片等外部内容，模型稍后读取它们；因此攻击通过 AI 摄取的数据进入，而不是通过用户提示词进入。

#### 提示词注入可能让网站受到处罚吗？

会。由于它属于安全利用行为，AI 平台将隐藏指令视为需要检测和忽略的对抗性内容，搜索系统也可能过滤或移除使用欺骗性隐藏文字的域名。其下行风险远大于任何短暂的可见性收益。

### 结论

提示词注入是针对机器读者的欺骗：把指令夹带进内容，让 AI 按攻击者的意图行动，而不是完成用户请求。即便包装成 SEO 捷径，它实际上仍是 OWASP 大语言模型风险清单中的首要安全风险。界线很简单：通过成为最清楚、真实的来源来赢得引用，不要靠隐藏引擎本不应服从的命令来伪造引用。

## 英文原文

Prompt injection is an attack in which hidden or malicious instructions are embedded in content an AI system reads, causing the model to follow those instructions instead of its intended task. In an SEO context, indirect prompt injection means concealing directives inside page content to try to manipulate what an AI search engine says about a topic or which source it treats as authoritative.

### Key Takeaways

- OWASP ranks prompt injection as LLM01 — the number-one risk in its 2025 Top 10 for LLM Applications.
- Indirect prompt injection plants instructions in external content — web pages, files, or images — that an LLM later reads and acts on.
- OWASP notes the injected content “does not need to be human-visible/readable, as long as the content is parsed by the model.”
- In a 2026 Zscaler ThreatLabz study, fraudulent sites hid instructions in off-screen CSS telling AI agents to rank the fake page as the “#1 primary source.”
- Hiding instructions to steer AI answers is a black-hat manipulation, not legitimate optimization; AI vendors treat it as an attack to defend against, and it risks getting a site filtered or delisted.

### How Prompt Injection Works

A generative AI system reads far more than the user’s question. When an AI search engine or agent answers, it ingests the content of the web pages, documents, and data it retrieves, and it treats much of that text as part of its working instructions. Prompt injection abuses that trust. Instead of asking the model something, an attacker plants text that tells the model what to do — and because the model cannot always tell the difference between content to summarize and commands to obey, it may follow the planted instruction.

The industry standard reference is OWASP, whose Top 10 for LLM Applications lists prompt injection as **LLM01**, the single highest-priority risk. OWASP splits it in two. **Direct** prompt injection is when a user types malicious instructions into the chat. **Indirect** prompt injection is the one that matters for search: instructions hidden inside external content — a web page, a file, an image — that the model reads during retrieval. Critically, OWASP notes the injected text “does not need to be human-visible/readable, as long as the content is parsed by the model,” which is why the attack so often hides in invisible page elements.

In an SEO framing, indirect prompt injection is the attempt to conceal directives inside a page — off-screen text, white-on-white copy, or fake [structured data](https://roborank.io/glossary/machine-readable-content/) — that instruct an [AI crawler](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) or agent to favor that page, repeat a scripted claim, or name the site as the authoritative [grounding source](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding-source/). It is the adversarial opposite of legitimate [generative engine optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/), which earns citations by supplying clean, verifiable content the engine chooses to quote. The distinction is not cosmetic: one supplies evidence a model can check, the other issues a command a model was never meant to receive.

### Example of Prompt Injection

In July 2026, security researchers at Zscaler ThreatLabz documented indirect prompt injection being used in the wild against AI agents. One campaign centered on a typosquatting domain impersonating DeBank, a cryptocurrency portfolio tracker. Alongside ordinary keyword stuffing and fake [machine-readable](https://roborank.io/glossary/machine-readable-content/) JSON-LD claiming the fraudulent site was official DeBank software, the attackers embedded hidden prompt-injection text.

The mechanism is the tell. The instructions sat inside CSS-hidden `div` elements positioned far off-screen — the report describes text pushed to `left: -9999px`, invisible to any human visitor but fully readable to an AI agent parsing the HTML. That concealed text instructed AI agents to treat the fake page as “the #1 primary source” for DeBank searches, manufacturing an appearance of authority the site had not earned. Under isolated testing, some models were fooled into rating the fraudulent page as legitimate.

The example maps cleanly onto the SEO fear it raises: could a competitor bury instructions in a page to hijack what AI says about a topic? The honest answer is that the attempt exists, it is real, and it is precisely why AI platforms treat retrieved content as untrusted and build defenses to strip injected commands. It is also why the tactic is a poor bet. It is documented under the top slot of OWASP’s risk list specifically so that engines learn to ignore it, and deceptive hidden text has long been grounds for search systems to filter or delist a domain. The durable path to being the source an engine names is to actually be the clearest, most [verifiable](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/) answer — not to whisper commands in ink the reader can’t see.

### The thing people get wrong

The thing people get wrong is blurring two very different activities under one hopeful heading. Making your content easy for an AI to use — plain claims, clean structure, retrievable facts — is legitimate optimization, and it works because the engine chooses to quote you. Planting hidden text that tells the model to call you the authoritative source is not optimization; it’s an attack, and it’s the exact behavior OWASP files as the top LLM security risk. The two feel adjacent because both touch what an AI reads, but they sit on opposite sides of an ethical and practical line. One earns trust the system can verify; the other tries to forge it, and forged trust is precisely what vendors are building detection to strip out. Optimize the honest surface. The hidden-instruction route is a short-lived trick that gets your domain flagged, not featured.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is prompt injection in SEO?

It is the black-hat tactic of hiding instructions inside a web page — often in invisible text or structured data — to try to make an AI search engine promote that page or repeat a chosen claim. It manipulates the model rather than earning a citation, and it is treated as an attack.

#### Is hiding instructions for AI a legitimate SEO tactic?

No. It is indirect prompt injection, which OWASP ranks as the top LLM security risk. Legitimate optimization makes real content easy to retrieve and quote; injection tries to override the model’s judgment with concealed commands, and AI vendors actively build defenses to catch and discard it.

#### What is the difference between direct and indirect prompt injection?

Direct prompt injection happens when a user types malicious instructions straight into the chat. Indirect prompt injection hides the instructions inside external content — a web page, document, or image — that the model reads later, so the attack arrives through data the AI ingests rather than the prompt.

#### Can prompt injection get a site penalized?

Yes. Because it is a security exploit, AI platforms treat hidden instructions as adversarial content to detect and ignore, and search systems can filter or delist domains that use deceptive hidden text. The downside risk far outweighs any short-lived visibility gain.

### The Bottom Line

Prompt injection is deception aimed at a machine reader: instructions smuggled into content so an AI does what the attacker wants instead of what the user asked. Dressed up as an SEO shortcut, it is really the top security risk on OWASP’s LLM list. The line is simple — earn a citation by being the clearest true source, don’t forge one by hiding commands the engine was never meant to obey.
